title: Hong Kong students navigating cross-boundary internships, exchange, and identity when studying or working in the Greater Bay Area
topic_description: Universities and employers promote Greater Bay placements as career bridges. Students encounter contracts, Putonghua business registers, and nuanced identity questions. Your discussion group includes local and non-local classmates. Debate whether GBA experience should be incentivised or remain optional, how institutions should safeguard labour rights and wellbeing, and how to discuss identity without reducing classmates to stereotypes.
instructions: You have 1 minute to prepare and 8 minutes for the group discussion (10 minutes for a group of 4). You should interact with your fellow candidates. Do not read out prepared notes. You may make notes during the preparation time, but you should not write out everything you plan to say.
discussion_points: Incentives versus coercion: scholarships, credits, and the ethics of ‘expecting’ GBA mobility.
Contract transparency: overtime, harassment protocols, bilingual documentation—what schools and hosts owe students.
Inclusive discussion norms: validating diverse identity experiences without competitive suffering narratives.
individual_response_questions: Should Hong Kong law require standard bilingual internship contracts for all publicly funded outbound placements?
How can English classrooms facilitate candid discussion of GBA opportunities without privileging one identity outcome?
hkeaa_alignment: Paper 4: sustained exchange on sensitive socio-political topics; language range for abstraction; discourse strategies for disagreement and repair.
success_feedback: You navigated identity–labour intersection issues with interactional care.
suggested_next_steps: Record 1 min on contract transparency; trim filler words.
